quizzes.title: Node Basics Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction & Modules, npm & the File System, HTTP & a First Server.

questions.prompt: What does this program print, in order?
questions.explanation: The normal code (A and C) runs first. The timer callback runs later through the event loop, even with a delay of 0.

questions.prompt: Which line imports a default export called greet from ./greet.js?
questions.explanation: A default export is imported without curly braces. For your own files you must also write the .js extension.

questions.prompt: Which file should you NOT commit to Git?
questions.explanation: node_modules can be rebuilt at any time with npm install, and it is very large. package.json and the lock file describe how to rebuild it.
path.extname returns the extension of the file name, including the dot.

questions.prompt: Fill in the method that sends the body and finishes the response.
questions.explanation: res.end(body) sends the body and finishes the response. Without it the client keeps waiting.

questions.prompt: A client asks for a page that does not exist. Which status code should your server send?
questions.explanation: 404 means Not Found. 500 is for bugs on the server, 200 means OK and 201 means Created.

quizzes.title: Express Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Express Routing, Middleware, Building a REST API.

questions.prompt: A client sends GET /users/42. What does this route send back?
questions.explanation: Route parameters are always strings, so req.params.id is the string "42" and JSON shows it in quotes.

questions.prompt: Which request reads the value of page in req.query.page?
questions.explanation: The query string comes after a question mark in the URL: ?page=2.

questions.prompt: This middleware never calls next() and never sends a response. What happens to the request?
options: The request hangs and never finishes
questions.explanation: Middleware must either call next() or send a response. Doing neither leaves the client waiting.

questions.prompt: Fill in the built-in middleware that parses JSON request bodies.
questions.explanation: express.json() reads a JSON body and puts it in req.body.

questions.prompt: Which status code is best after a POST request successfully creates a new book?
questions.explanation: 201 Created tells the client that a new resource was made. 204 is used for success with no body, such as delete.

questions.prompt: How does Express know a function is an error-handling middleware?
options: It has four parameters (err, req, res, next)
It is placed first in the file
questions.explanation: Express counts the parameters. Four parameters mean error handler, and it should be registered after the routes.

quizzes.title: Databases & Security Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: MongoDB & Mongoose, Authentication: bcrypt, JWT, httpOnly cookies, protecting routes, .env.

questions.prompt: In MongoDB, what is the equivalent of a row in an SQL table?
questions.explanation: A document is one record, like a row. A collection (like a table) holds many documents.

questions.prompt: What is the value of student.name after this code?
questions.explanation: The trim option removes spaces at both ends when Mongoose casts the value.

questions.prompt: Fill in the keyword so the new value is saved before the next line runs.
questions.explanation: Mongoose methods return promises. Without await you would get a query object, not the list of students.

questions.prompt: Why do we store a bcrypt hash instead of the password?
options: A hash cannot be turned back into the password, so a database leak is less dangerous
questions.explanation: A hash is one-way. bcrypt is also deliberately slow and adds a salt, which makes guessing passwords hard.

questions.prompt: What does the httpOnly flag on a cookie do?
options: Sends the cookie only over HTTPS
Stops JavaScript in the page from reading the cookie
Stops the browser from sending the cookie
questions.explanation: httpOnly hides the cookie from document.cookie, so a script injected into the page cannot steal the token. The browser still sends it with requests.

questions.prompt: What does this middleware do when the cookie is missing?
options: Calls next() and shows the profile
Sends 401 and the route handler does not run
questions.explanation: It returns a 401 response and does not call next(), so the protected handler is never reached.
